changes.before: Repair offerMessage(member) so the outer message changes for a member and stays Standard access otherwise.
changes.after: Update an existing name from inside a block instead of creating a separate inner name.

before: A block is a group of statements inside braces, such as the body of an if statement.
A name declared with let or const belongs to its block. An inner block can use a name from an outer block.
A const binding also belongs to its block, but cannot be reassigned. Use let when this binding needs a new value.
An inner name is not available outside its block. Reading a name before its let or const declaration runs also causes an error; do not treat it as an empty value.
For the practice, decide whether you need to create another message or update the message that the return statement reads.
after: A block groups instructions inside braces. An `if` branch is one kind of block.
A name created with `let` or `const` belongs to its block. Code in a block can also use names from blocks around it.
`const` also belongs to its block, but its name cannot be assigned a new value. Use `let` when you need to change the value.
A name created inside a block cannot be used outside that block. Trying to read a `let` or `const` name before its declaration runs also causes an error.
`return message` reads the outer message. Update that message inside the `if` block instead of declaring a second one.

before: Repair offerMessage(member) so the outer message changes for a member and stays Standard access otherwise.
Change one case and explain the result.
after: Remove that `let` so assignment updates the existing message.
Check that other users still get `"Standard access"`.

before.question: let color="blue"; if (true) { let color="gold"; } console.log(color); What changes if you remove only the inner let?
choices: The final log changes from blue to gold
Nothing changes; the two names always refer to one binding
The final log changes from gold to blue
before.explanation: With let, the inner declaration shadows the outer binding. Without let, assignment updates the existing outer color, so the final log reads gold.

choices: Nothing changes; the two names always share one value.
The final output changes from gold to blue.
after.explanation: Without the inner `let`, assignment updates the outer color. The final line then prints gold.

before: The return statement reads the message declared in the function body.
Decide whether the if block should declare a new binding or assign to the existing one.
after: The return reads the message declared before the `if`.
A second `let` creates a separate name; assignment alone updates the existing one.

project.title: Names inside a block
project.task: Fix `offerMessage` so a member gets `"Member access"` and everyone else gets `"Standard access"`.
project.done_when: Both cases pass, and you can explain why the inner assignment updates the outer message.
